newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market slow - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market slow - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Wednesday were slow, with thin sales of lightweight steers and heifers reported, feedlot sources said.
About 1,000 lightweight heifers in Kansas and about 3,000 steers and heifers in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area sold at $68.00 in a light market test, they said.
"From what I could see, they weren't front-end but second-set cattle, and the trade was not real widespread," a Kansas feedlot manager said.
The sales reportedly were below the quality of the bulk of last week's cattle that sold at $69.00, the sources said.
Further bids at $68.00 were passed by owners continuing to ask $70.00 for heavier-weight cattle, feedlot sources said.
However, lower beef prices this week could pull the rest of cattle down $1.00 from last week's trade, they said.
Beef prices were pressured by a buildup of beef stocks following last week's large cattle slaughter last week.
Midday beef prices were quoted down $0.06 to $0.96 per cwt, with 271 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported.
Heavyweight choice beef was down $0.06 at $106.29, compared with Tuesday and down $0.68 since Friday's close, USDA statistics showed.
